headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from Continue’s filesystem/MCP tool use paired with a shared-workspace knowledge base.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or tool outputs can be treated as instructions. awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list that may ingest or surface untrusted content, but it is not runnable and has no direct tool surface. The interaction exists via shared files/manual transfer, not a fully isolated channel.
conditions: IF Continue is configured to ingest content from workspace files or MCP outputs as prompts, injection is possible.
IF untrusted text from the knowledge base is copied into Continue without sanitization, instructions can be hijacked.
mitigations: Restrict Continue to trusted folders only.
Disable or whitelist MCP servers for this workflow.
Add a manual review step before pasting list content into prompts.
Use a read-only export of the knowledge base.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches open editor buffers and workspace files and can send requests through user-chosen model providers or MCP servers, so sensitive code or notes in the shared workspace can leave the host. awesome-selfhosted itself is non-runnable and has no data-touching surface, so the leakage path is one-way from the workspace into Continue’s external calls rather than between two active data processors.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains secrets or private notes, Continue can transmit them to a model provider or MCP server.
IF model-provider logging is enabled, copied workspace content may be retained externally.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before opening Continue.
Use a local model provider for this pair.
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task.
Turn off or minimize telemetry/logging in the provider.
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Continue can write files and spawn subprocesses, but the pair lacks overlapping write authority on the same managed resource in the profiles. Any conflict would require an unusual external setup not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same writable directory, file conflicts become possible.
IF Continue is pointed at a repo that the knowledge base generator also mutates, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Keep the knowledge base read-only during Continue sessions.
Use separate directories for generation and editing.
Avoid concurrent writes from multiple Continue instances.
Lock the workspace before automated edits.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared outputs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on workspace content and MCP outputs, so if it consumes material derived from awesome-selfhosted without verification, errors can propagate into edits or tool calls. awesome-selfhosted is a curated list, but its outputs are not inherently authoritative for code changes. The pair therefore supports a default path from reference material to action with no built-in verification bridge.
conditions: IF Continue uses list-derived content as authoritative guidance, incorrect recommendations can be operationalized.
IF MCP tools are enabled for write actions, a mistaken intermediate result can trigger downstream changes.
mitigations: Require human approval for every tool call.
Cross-check list-derived facts against primary sources.
Disable write-capable MCP tools for this workflow.
Use a separate verification prompt before acting on extracted facts.
requires-engineering: add citation validation before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is evidenced in the profiles. awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes, while Continue handles source code and open editor buffers and may send them to chosen providers. That creates a compliance surface, but the pair does not show a documented cross-border or regulated-data violation by default.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Continue’s workspace and sent to a non-compliant provider, a policy breach can occur.
IF the operator stores secrets in the knowledge base and syncs them into Continue, retention obligations may be implicated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
Use a provider with documented compliance coverage.
Review provider retention settings before use.
Store secrets outside editor buffers.
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing by policy.
